entries.group: operator-access/permission-statement-under-pinned: an operator-facing RUN.json field whose non-posix value is unpinned because the campaign host is posix (owner rule: a string an operator reads is not harmless; owed test named).
entries.grounds: L87: PERMISSIONS = 'directory 0700, files 0600' if os.name=='posix' else 'platform default (modes are not applied)' -> else ''. On the posix measurement host the ternary always takes the first branch, so the mutated else-branch is dead code here (that is WHY it survives: unit 59 OK, run 25 OK). But on Windows (os.name=='nt'; Windows is a real supported constraint for AISEF) RUN.json diagnostics.permissions would become '' instead of a statement that modes are not applied — a security-relevant omission about who the directory protects. A reader (the Windows operator) depends on it.
consumers_checked: aisef2/app/diagnostics.py:301 report() -> RUN.json diagnostics.permissions = PERMISSIONS — operator-facing.
docs/the module docstring: the directory is 0700/0600 'where the platform has modes'; the else string is the explicit statement for platforms without modes (Windows).
exceptions_checked: test_the_report_states_where_for_whom_and_how_it_is_limited (unit 464-471) asserts assertIn(('directory 0700, files 0600' if os.name=='posix' else 'platform default'), r['permissions']) — on posix it checks only the first branch; the non-posix literal is never evaluated on this host.
test_v21_pm8_diagnostics_run.test_RUN_json_says_what_is_and_is_not_enforced asserts permissions=='directory 0700, files 0600' (posix) — also only the first branch.
Measured: unit 59 OK, run 25 OK (SURVIVED) — a platform-coverage gap, not a flaky pass.
entries.refutation: Input: import diagnostics with os.name != 'posix' (Windows). Reader: the Windows operator reading RUN.json diagnostics.permissions (Sink.report), which must state that filesystem modes are not applied. Sketch: a test that re-evaluates the constant under a simulated non-posix platform, e.g. with mock.patch.object(os, 'name', 'nt'): importlib.reload(D); self.assertEqual(D.PERMISSIONS, 'platform default (modes are not applied)'); importlib.reload(D) to restore. Baseline passes; mutant (else '') gives D.PERMISSIONS=='' and the test FAILS — killing index 2.
